drafts.rationale: Lightest feasible design found. Passes REQ-001 to REQ-007 at nominal and in the REQ-006 worst case (2750 N, 29.5 mm). t/w = 2.00 is at the REQ-007 limit.
Passes all requirements. Ultimate margin in the REQ-006 worst case is only about +0.007, so it has little headroom.
Passes all requirements with lower t/w (0.62) and more margin than the lighter options.
Most conservative of the four. Passes all requirements, with t/w = 0.32 and the largest stiffness margin among these options.

Lightest feasible point. Stiffness governs (REQ-003/006). Worst case (2750 N, 19.5 mm) gives yield MS +0.39, ultimate MS +0.17, deflection 2.98 mm. Width 11 mm fails REQ-006 (3.25 mm), so 12 mm is the minimum at 20 mm thickness. Passes REQ-004/005/007 (t/w 1.67).
Slightly wider than the lightest point for extra stiffness margin. Worst case gives yield MS +0.45, deflection 2.86 mm. Passes all requirements, t/w 1.60.
Thicker plate gives much larger stiffness margin. Worst case gives yield MS +1.29, deflection 1.44 mm. t/w is exactly 2.00, at the REQ-007 limit. Passes all requirements.
Alternative thickness. Worst case gives yield MS +0.76, ultimate MS +0.48, deflection 2.97 mm. Heavier than the 20 mm options. Passes all requirements, t/w 0.67.
Lightest passing design. Yield stress 269 MPa nominal (MS +0.29). Worst case REQ-006 (2750 N, 24.5 mm) gives MS +0.13 and 0.80 mm. t/w = 2.00, at the REQ-007 limit. Stock thickness 25 mm.
Same thickness with 0.5 mm more width for more margin. Worst case REQ-006 gives MS +0.18 and 0.77 mm. t/w = 1.92, so REQ-007 holds with some slack.
Alternative using 20 mm stock. Nominal MS +0.16. Worst case REQ-006 gives MS +0.00 and 1.13 mm, which is marginal but passes. t/w = 1.14.
Thinner, wider section for a different trade-off. Nominal MS +0.19. Worst case REQ-006 gives MS +0.01 and 1.41 mm. t/w = 0.57. Heavier than the 25 mm options.

attacks.title: REQ-006 stack: load +10% and plate 0.5 mm thinner
attacks.rationale: Requirement case itself. Yield MS 0.391, ultimate MS 0.173, but tip deflection 2.981 mm against a 3.0 mm limit, leaving 0.6% headroom. Passes on paper, no practical margin.

attacks.title: Machining removes 1 mm from thickness (20 to 19 mm)
attacks.rationale: Plausible finishing or surface-prep loss. Deflection rises to 2.93 mm (about 17% increase, consistent with 1/t^3 scaling). Still passes, with only about 2% deflection headroom.

attacks.title: Layout change lengthens arm by 20 mm (140 to 160 mm)
attacks.rationale: A realistic layout change. Deflection goes to 3.75 mm, failing REQ-003 by 25%. Scaling suggests nominal-load failure above about 148.6 mm, so the allowable growth is only about 8.6 mm.

attacks.title: Width loses 2 mm in machining (12 to 10 mm)
attacks.rationale: Deflection 3.014 mm, failing REQ-003 by 0.01 mm. Ultimate MS drops to 0.131. Also brings REQ-007 (t/w <= 2) to exactly 2.0. Nominal-load failure threshold is a width loss of about 1.9 mm.

attacks.title: Stacked realistic change: load +10%, plate -0.5 mm, width -1 mm, arm +10 mm
attacks.rationale: Combined tolerance and layout drift. Deflection 4.00 mm (33% over limit). Ultimate MS falls to 0.003, effectively zero. Shows the design has no margin for combined changes.

events.rule: a redesign needs a blocking finding
events.rationale: The shipped 12 x 20 mm Ti-6Al-4V part passes the stated requirements, but G-04 shows that a realistic stacked change (load +10%, plate -0.5 mm, width -1 mm, arm +10 mm) pushes tip deflection to about 4.0 mm, which breaks REQ-003, and a 20 mm arm change alone does the same. Deflection, not yield, is the governing constraint (yield margin is about +0.6 nominal), so the stiffness must be raised while keeping REQ-007 satisfied, and G-01 to G-03 confirm the margin is too thin to accept without that change.

events.summary: The Ti-6Al-4V 12 x 20 mm bracket passes all six structural, material-performance and fabrication rules (S-01 to S-06, M-02 to M-04, F-01 to F-03), but design allowables (M-01), dissimilar-metal joint specification (M-05), fracture control classification (X-01), fatigue analysis (X-02) and supplier/procurement items (P-01 to P-03) remain open actions. Export control (P-04) is informational and not determined, so no status has been changed.
top_risks: M-01 and S-01 to S-03: margins rely on typical handbook values, so the pass results are not valid until MMPDS A- or B-basis allowables for this alloy, temper and thickness are substituted.
X-02 and X-01: fatigue under launch vibration is not analyzed and fracture control classification is not recorded, leaving cyclic loading and fracture criticality unverified.
M-05 and P-01 to P-03: galvanic corrosion at the joint is unaddressed and the specialty metal origin, heat-lot traceability and AS9100 vendor requirements are not yet satisfied by the supply chain.

actions.action: Replace typical values with MMPDS A- or B-basis allowables for Ti-6Al-4V in the specified temper and thickness, then rerun S-01 to S-03.
Perform fatigue analysis using program cyclic load cases, including launch vibration, and report the result against the program standard.
Classify the bracket fracture control category (for example non-fracture-critical) and record the rationale in the compliance file.
Specify fastener material and finish at the joint to mitigate galvanic corrosion per MIL-STD-889.
Confirm the specialty metal melt origin is the US or a qualifying country under DFARS 252.225-7009 and obtain vendor attestation.
